description: Figure 10 is a grouped bar chart illustrating the “effect” of context masking on case-related tasks, with results grouped by language family and shown for multiple multilingual BERT model variants. The horizontal axis contains the language-family categories in left-to-right order: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis is labeled “effect” and uses a linear scale with labeled ticks at approximately 0, 10, 20, and 30 (with the plotted range extending slightly below 0 and up to the mid-30s). Within each language-family group, six adjacent bars are shown (a clustered arrangement) corresponding to the legend entries mBERT-L2 (light blue), XLM-L2 (medium blue), mBERT-R2 (light green), XLM-R2 (dark green), mBERT-B2 (pink), and XLM-B2 (red); each bar includes a vertical error bar indicating standard deviation. Approximate bar heights by group are: IE-Baltic shows small positive effects (roughly ~1–6) across all six bars; IE-Germanic shows blue bars around ~9–10, green bars near ~0, and pink/red bars around ~14–15; IE-Indic shows the largest cluster overall with green bars around ~20–22 and pink/red bars around ~21–24, while the blue bars are near ~0–1; IE-Romance shows moderate values with blue bars around ~5–7, green bars near ~0, and pink/red around ~10–12; IE-Slavic family shows blue bars around ~9–10, green near ~0, and pink/red around ~16–18; IE-other shows blue around ~5–6, green near ~0, and pink/red around ~7–8; Isolate shows values close to zero (roughly ~0–2) for all colors; Semitic shows higher blue bars (about ~12 and ~16), green bars slightly below or near zero (around ~-2 to ~0), and pink/red around ~15–20; Uralic shows small positive effects (roughly ~1–3) across bars. The bars are not visually sorted by magnitude (they follow the fixed language-family order), and no individual bars appear specially emphasized beyond the consistent color coding and the presence of error bars.
